category_description: How income tax, GST and capital gains tax work in Australia.
subcategory_description: The tax-free threshold, resident tax rates and the Medicare levy.
label: Tax-free threshold for a full-year resident
context: Most Australian residents for tax purposes can claim it on the first part of their income in an income year. Claiming it reduces the tax withheld from pay.

subject_intro: How much income Australian residents can earn before paying income tax, how to claim the threshold from an employer, and how it works for part of a year.
subject_meta_description: Australian residents can earn {fact:au_tax_free_threshold} a year before income tax applies. How to claim it from an employer, and how part-year residents are treated.
label: Part-year tax-free threshold: flat amount
context: For someone who is an Australian resident for tax purposes for only part of an income year. An extra amount is added, worked out from the months spent in Australia.

label: Part-year tax-free threshold: most the extra amount can be
context: Pro-rated by the number of months in Australia during the income year, including the month of arrival.
